  - region "Simple English explanation of Triangle Area Formula":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Triangle Area Formula" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "The trigonometric triangle area formula uses two sides and the included angle. In Triangle Area Formula, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Trig area: A=(1/2)ab sin C. You can learn Triangle Area Formula by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Choose two sides with the angle between them. Substitute into one half ab sin C. Keep square units. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, land area: Two boundary lengths and included angle can find area. Watch out: Using an angle that is not between the two sides. Use the included angle."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Find the labelled triangle area formula for base 3 and height 4.

    - generic: The two methods match.
    - text: The altitude is the perpendicular component of either adjacent side, so 1/2 ab sin C equals 1/2 base × height.
  - article:
    - heading "Formula / Rule" [level=2]:
      - text: Formula / Rule
    - paragraph: For any triangle with sides a and b including angle C between them,
    - strong: A = 1/2 ab sin C
    - paragraph: Where
    - list:
      - listitem: a, b are the two sides
      - listitem: C is the included angle between a and b
      - listitem: A is the area of the triangle
    - generic: "Domain: 0° < C < 180°"
    - generic: "Sign: sin C > 0 in this domain, so A > 0"
  - article:
    - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]:
      - text: Worked Example
    - paragraph: Find the area of a triangle with a = 7, b = 9, and included angle C = 60°.
    - heading "Solution" [level=3]
    - strong:
      - text: A = 1/2 ab sin C
      - text: = 1/2 (7)(9) sin 60°
      - text: = 31.5 × √3/2
      - text: = 27.28 square units
  - article:
    - heading "Common Misconception" [level=2]:
      - text: Common Misconception
    - paragraph: Do not use the angle opposite a side.
    - strong: 1/2 ab sin C uses the angle C included between sides a and b.
    - paragraph: Using any other angle gives the wrong area.
